text:
Mira: Heads-up — ran the nightly candidate-kernel sweep against h100/ampere stacks, trying the new arch-aware pick logic. Putting the raw output here and need quick triage.
Alex: thx, drop it here. any regressions or big wins?
Mira: summary first: most kernels stable, but one candidate (k-cand-42) shows 6-9% p99 regression on Ampere for seqlen=512 when KV cache warm. H100 looks fine.
Jordan: interesting, did autotuner pick a different codepath for >256? we added the seqlen cutoff recently.
Mira: yes — autotune chose path B (vectorized reduction) for >256 on ampere. path A (loop-unroll) is still used on h100.
Sam: can you paste the failing microbench command?
Mira: sure: ```./kbench --kernel k-cand-42 --arch ampere --seqs 32,128,256,512 --kvcache warm --iters 1000 --trace p99```
Lina: quick note: ampere's L2 behavior around 512 can flip performance for vectorized reductions. might be a cache-line thrash.
perf-bot: nightly-kbench: k-cand-42 @ ampere seqlen=512 p99 +8.1% (regression) — CI ID: nkb-2026-03-17-07. logs: https://ci.internal/reports/nkb-2026-03-17-07
Alex: okay looks reproducible. is this specific to warm KV or also cold?
Mira: only warm KV shows the regression. cold KV looks neutral (+0.4%).
Jordan: that points to KV cache interaction — maybe the new path touches KV layout differently and invalidates more lines.
Sam: can we repro with perf counters? collect L2_MISS, LLC_REFERENCES, and CPI.
Mira: ran perf-collected sample: ```L2_MISS +22% at seq512, LLC_REF +10%, CPI +4%```
Lina: yep, L2 miss increase aligns with thrash theory. For ampere we should fallback to path A for seq>=512 when kv_warm=true until we dig deeper.
Alex: propose a quick patch to autotuner: add an override rule: if arch==ampere && kv_warm && seqlen>=512 => prefer path A. Low risk and buys time.
Jordan: agree, but also add a microprobe to the CI that exercises KV-warm long sequences to avoid regressions.
Mira: I'll open a PR with the override and a new microprobe test. PR will include the kernel repro script and perf counter collection.
perf-bot: perf-presubmit: new microprobe test queued (id: probe-ampere-kv512). Expect results in ~30m.
Sam: for the autotuner change, consider adding a metric threshold rather than hard cutoff — e.g., prefer A if L2_MISS increase > 12% during discovery.
Alex: true, but discovery runs are noisy. for now hard override is OK, add a ticket to refine with metrics.
Lina: also logging idea: record the chosen codepath + KV state in kbench metadata so nightly diffs can correlate.
Mira: done — I added `codepath=...` and `kv_state=warm|cold` to the kbench JSON output.
Jordan: after the override lands, can we re-run the nightly sweep on a canary pool for 3 nights to ensure no other arch-specific flips?
Mira: yes will schedule a 3-night canary and post summary.
ops-bot: deploy-plan: autotune-override PR -> canary pool (n=3 runs) -> full roll if no regressions.
Alex: thanks all. Lina — you ok to lead the deeper probe into vectorized reduction memory access pattern?
Lina: on it. I'll add a microprobe that dumps addresses and stride patterns under seq=512.
Mira: final note: adding these targeted microprobes to perf CI should reduce future surprises. Will update the engineering playbook after PR merges. :+1:
Sam: cheers, thanks Mira for the triage dump.
perf-bot: nightly-kbench: probe-ampere-kv512 finished — result: reproducible regression confirmed. Details posted in nkb-2026-03-17-07.
Mira: closing this thread once PR merges and canary completes. will post follow-up results.
